text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a development practice where team members regularly merge their code changes into a shared main branch. The key to CI is automation: every time new code is pushed, a CI pipeline automatically triggers a build and runs a series of tests. This process helps catch issues early, before they become bigger problems. Instead of discovering a broken feature days later, developers are alerted within minutes. This saves time and reduces stress, as fixing a small bug is much simpler than debugging a large, tangled mess. Ultimately, CI pipelines ensure that the software remains in a stable, working state at all times.
